domain_label: Question Craft & Answering — Directive Answering Strategy (INBDE one-best-answer MC + TOEFL iBT task types)
purpose: A method for answering exam items well: key the procedure to the format actually in front of the learner, read stem-first, predict-then-eliminate against engineered distractors, work INBDE itemsets/cases off a once-scanned Patient Box, budget time per item type from the official counts, and drive TOEFL productive tasks off note templates — stating the sourced structural facts (INBDE one-best-answer MC, no guessing penalty, TOEFL 2026 dropping integrated tasks) as fact and tagging every answering-craft tactic an estimate.
assumptions: no observed learner-timing dataset is supplied; every per-item time budget is a heuristic craft split derived from official item counts and section times, not a measured sell-through of the learner's own pace
the two target exams are the INBDE (JCNDE/ADA, US dental exam for foreign graduates) and the TOEFL iBT (ETS), pinned in the sibling research files exam_dental_us_fmg.md and exam_toefl.md

the sandbox egress proxy blocked direct reads of jcnde.ada.org, ets.org and nbme.org this session, so every [FACT] is verified through search-engine excerpts quoting the named official page, not the page body — the tactic layer is craft synthesis on top of those facts

the learner's practice bank still contains legacy (2023-2025) TOEFL integrated material even though the live 2026 test dropped it, so both the current-format and legacy templates are carried and format-gated
answering craft is generalizable test-strategy practice (predict-then-eliminate, flag-and-move, note templates) applied to these two exams, not a claim about any individual item's key
exclusions: item-authoring craft (writing stems, distractors, cover-the-options construction, flaw avoidance) beyond using the writer's flaw taxonomy as an answerer's tiebreaker — that belongs to the item-writing specialist

question-bank metadata and psychometrics (p-value, point-biserial, discrimination index, IRT b/a/c calibration, distractor analysis) beyond reading an item's difficulty/Bloom level to pick effort — that belongs to the bank-metadata specialist

the exam blueprints, content-area enumerations, registration, scoring-scale mechanics and scheduling beyond the per-item time budget and the no-guessing-penalty fact — those belong to the exam-identity specialists
stating a fabricated pass rate, exact per-type item count, section time or wrong-answer penalty that the research file did not verify
subject-matter knowledge (dental clinical content, English vocabulary/grammar) that the answering procedure operates on but does not itself supply

competency_questions.question: Why must the answering procedure be keyed to the format actually in front of the learner, and what does the INBDE one-best-answer model guarantee?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_KEYING states the strategy must match the exam+format+stimulus in front of the user (INBDE standalone/itemset/case MC vs TOEFL task types, legacy vs 2026) and ONE_BEST_ANSWER_MODEL states the INBDE is exclusively one-best-answer MC with 3-5 choices and exactly one best option as a FACT

competency_questions.question: How are distractors engineered, and why can a plausible-sounding option not be trusted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISTRACTOR_ENGINEERING states distractors are written homogeneous with and directly related to the lead-in to be plausible to the non-master (NBME canon, FACT via excerpts), so a sounds-right option is not evidence of correctness

competency_questions.question: In what order should a single-best-answer stem be read, and why lead-in first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STEM_FIRST_READING prescribes reading the lead-in (last line) first then the vignette so the learner knows which data matters while reading, tags the tactic an estimate, and ANSWER_BEFORE_LOOKING sets up the predict move

competency_questions.question: Why commit a predicted answer before viewing the options, and how does elimination take over when no prediction is possible?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANSWER_BEFORE_LOOKING states committing a prediction then matching immunizes against engineered distractors (the cover-the-options rule inverted), and SYSTEMATIC_ELIMINATION strikes options that are true-but-non-responsive, internally false, or heterogeneous

competency_questions.question: How should writer-flaw testwiseness cues be used, and why only as tiebreakers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TESTWISENESS_TIEBREAKERS names absolute-term options, the grammatical odd-one-out and the longest/most-detailed option as cues from the NBME flaw taxonomy usable only as tiebreakers because a well-built exam is scrubbed of them, and SYSTEMATIC_ELIMINATION remains the primary move

competency_questions.question: How are negative (EXCEPT/NOT) stems handled, and why is no item ever left blank on these exams?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEGATIVE_STEM_HANDLING rewrites a negative lead-in as mark-each-option-true/false-pick-the-false-one, and NO_GUESS_PENALTY_RULE states the INBDE has no guessing penalty (FACT) and TOEFL MC has no documented penalty (ESTIMATE), so a blank is never left

competency_questions.question: How are INBDE itemsets and cases worked off the Patient Box and image stimulus?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PATIENT_BOX_SCAN scans the box once systematically (demographics -> complaint -> meds/history -> findings) then treats it as a lookup table, CASE_CLUSTER_STRATEGY states items are independently scored so an earlier answer is never revised for consistency, and IMAGE_STIMULUS_ORIENT orients to the image (film type, region) before reading the question

competency_questions.question: How is the per-item time budget set on the INBDE, and when does the learner flag and move on?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIME_BUDGET_MODEL derives budgets from official item counts and section times, INBDE_TIME_BUDGET gives ~63 s/standalone and ~90-105 s/case item with the box-scan surplus, and FLAG_AND_MOVE sets a first-pass and a hard flag-and-move cap

competency_questions.question: How is the per-task time budget set on the TOEFL iBT?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOEFL_TIME_BUDGET gives ~1 min/question for the ~200-word academic passage, ~10 s/blank for Complete the Words using the intact first sentence, the one-hearing pre-focus for Listen and Choose a Response, and the ~10 min WAD split, all tagged estimate off the official counts

competency_questions.question: What note templates drive the current TOEFL productive tasks (WAD and Write an Email)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WAD_TEMPLATE gives the position -> reason+example -> engage-a-classmate-by-name -> optional concession structure at >=100 words, and EMAIL_TEMPLATE gives the register-matched greeting -> purpose -> 2 details/requests -> closing structure, both tagged estimate aligned to ETS scoring emphasis

competency_questions.question: What is the legacy integrated read-listen note grid, why is it legacy-only, and how is Listen and Repeat handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEGACY_INTEGRATED_GRID gives the two-column Reading|Lecture grid capturing the lecture's verb of opposition per row and states it applies only to pre-2026 practice material because the 2026 test dropped integrated tasks (FORMAT_KEYING), and LISTEN_REPEAT_TACTIC chunks the sentence prosodically to reproduce the stress pattern

competency_questions.question: How does reading an item's Bloom level shape effort, and how does the playbook compose format+stimulus+time into one answering procedure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BLOOM_LEVEL_READING reads whether an item is recall or apply/analyze (vignette+decision) and matches effort accordingly (FACT that format bounds level), and STRATEGY_SELECTION_PLAYBOOK composes the format, stimulus and time inputs into the selected read/eliminate/budget procedure

glossary.definition: The INBDE's exclusive item model: every item is multiple-choice with 3-5 answer choices where only one is the correct or best option; there is no select-all, ordering, drag-drop or hotspot format on the INBDE [FACT — INBDE Item Development & Candidate Guides via search excerpts].

The NBME item-writing test that a focused lead-in lets a reader cover the options and produce the answer unaided; the answerer inverts it into a solving move — predict the answer before looking, then match — to immunize against engineered distractors [FACT rule / ESTIMATE tactic].

Distractors are written to be homogeneous with the correct answer and directly related to the lead-in so they are plausible to a non-master; therefore an option sounding right is not evidence it is right [FACT — NBME Item-Writing Guide via excerpts].

A construction flaw that helps the savvy without knowledge: absolute-term options (always/never) usually wrong, the grammatical odd-one-out usually wrong, the longest/most-detailed option often keyed, stem-option word repeats; usable by an answerer only as a tiebreaker because a well-built exam is scrubbed of them [FACT taxonomy / ESTIMATE application].

The INBDE's standardized patient-summary table (demographics, chief complaint, history, findings) shared by an itemset or case; the answerer scans it once in clinical order, then uses it as a per-item lookup table rather than rereading it [FACT structure / ESTIMATE tactic].

INBDE grouped formats: an itemset is 3-6 items on a Patient Box only; a case is 3-6 items on a Patient Box plus an image or other stimulus (radiograph, photo, chart). Items in a set are independently scored [FACT format; independent-scoring ESTIMATE — standard construction].

The INBDE has no penalty for wrong answers (scaled score 49-99, pass 75) so every item is answered; TOEFL MC has no wrong-answer penalty documented in any source seen this session, so it is treated the same [INBDE FACT / TOEFL ESTIMATE].

The current-format TOEFL writing task: a professor's discussion prompt plus two classmate posts, to which the learner writes a ~100+ word contribution in ~10 min; scored on relevant contribution and engagement, not summary [FACT task / ESTIMATE template].

The pre-2026 TOEFL read-then-listen-then-write/speak tasks that the 2026 test dropped ('the test will no longer contain integrated questions. Nor will it contain an essay task', ETS via excerpt); the integrated note grid therefore applies only to legacy practice banks, which still dominate published prep [FACT drop / ESTIMATE that legacy prep dominates].

The craft rule that a stuck item is flagged and abandoned at a hard per-item cap (e.g. ~90 s on an INBDE standalone budgeted at ~63 s) rather than allowed to starve later items, then revisited if time remains [ESTIMATE — craft off the official time budget].

nodes.definition: Establish the root discipline: the answering procedure must be keyed to the item format actually in front of the learner, never to a remembered generic strategy. The two target exams differ sharply — the INBDE is exclusively one-best-answer multiple-choice (standalone, itemset or case) [FACT], while the TOEFL iBT is a spread of task types (single-answer MC, constrained text entry, spoken repetition/response, timed production) [FACT]; and the 2026 TOEFL dropped the legacy integrated tasks and the essay, so a task in front of the learner may be current-format or legacy-practice [FACT]. A question specialist keys strategy to the format because the same knowledge is tested through different mechanics: a select-3-of-6 prose summary, a one-best-answer vignette and a WAD each demand a different move. Read the exam, the format (standalone/itemset/case/task-type) and the stimulus (none/Patient Box/image/audio) before choosing any reading or elimination procedure.

included: identifying exam + format + stimulus before choosing a procedure
the INBDE-MC vs TOEFL-task-type contrast and the legacy-vs-2026 split as FACTs
keying strategy to the mechanics in front of the learner
excluded: the exam blueprint and content areas

pros.claim: Keying strategy to the actual format stops a learner drilling a procedure the item in front of them does not reward
pros.example: recognizing a select-3-of-6 prose-summary item needs a different move than a one-best-answer vignette before starting

cons.claim: The format map depends on official pages that were only reachable via search excerpts this session, so an exact per-type count can shift under the adaptive module
cons.example: treating a legacy taxonomy as current when the live 2026 test has re-shuffled the task mix

failure_modes: applying one generic MCQ routine to every format regardless of mechanics
drilling a legacy task type the current test no longer contains
acceptance_tests: the analysis identifies exam + format + stimulus first, states the INBDE-MC vs TOEFL-task-type contrast and the legacy-vs-2026 split as FACTs, and conditions the procedure choice on them
revisit_triggers: ETS or JCNDE publishes a format change to a target exam
the learner's bank shifts between legacy and current material
a new task type appears in the adaptive module

base.update_signal: an exam format change or a legacy-vs-current bank shift re-keys the strategy

nodes.definition: Fix the item model the INBDE reading strategy operates on: every INBDE item is one-best-answer multiple-choice with 3-5 answer choices, only one of which is the correct or best option, and options that are rankable on a single dimension with exactly one defensibly best answer [FACT — INBDE Candidate & Item Development Guides; NBME one-best-answer canon, via search excerpts]. Searches surfaced no multiple-response, ordering, drag-drop or hotspot format on the INBDE, so the answerer never expects a select-all move on it [FACT — negative finding]. This model is what makes predict-then-match viable: because exactly one option is best on one dimension, the learner can form an answer from the stem before reading options. It also bounds the TOEFL contrast — TOEFL does use a true multiple-response format (legacy prose-summary select-3-of-6), which the format-keying step flags separately.

included: the 3-5 choice one-best-answer INBDE model with exactly one best option on one dimension
the negative finding that the INBDE uses no select-all/ordering/hotspot format
why the model makes predict-then-match viable
excluded: TOEFL's own multiple-response legacy format detail

pros.claim: Knowing exactly one option is best on one dimension licenses forming an answer from the stem before reading options
pros.example: committing a predicted diagnosis from a vignette because the item cannot have two co-correct answers

cons.claim: The one-best-answer guarantee is verified via search excerpts of the official guides, not the guide bodies, and pretest items could in principle pilot other formats
cons.example: assuming an unscored pretest item is one-best-answer when its format is unstated in any excerpt seen

failure_modes: expecting a select-all move on an INBDE item that has exactly one best answer
treating two options as co-correct when the model forbids it
acceptance_tests: the model states 3-5 choices with exactly one best option on one dimension as FACT, carries the negative finding on absent formats, and links it to the predict-then-match move
revisit_triggers: JCNDE documents a new INBDE item format
a pretest item is confirmed to pilot a non-one-best format
the official guide body becomes fetchable to verify verbatim

base.update_signal: a new INBDE format or a verbatim guide verification updates the model

nodes.definition: Explain why an answerer cannot trust a plausible-sounding option: distractors are engineered. The NBME item-writing canon requires options to be homogeneous with the correct answer and directly related to the lead-in, all judged true/false on one dimension, so a good distractor is deliberately plausible to the non-master [FACT — NBME Item-Writing Guide via search excerpts]. The consequence for the answerer is the core of directive learning: a sounds-right feeling is exactly what the writer built, so it is not evidence of correctness. This is the reason predict-then-match beats read-and-recognize, and the reason elimination must be on responsiveness to the lead-in, not on surface plausibility. It also sets up the writer-flaw tiebreakers: where an exam is poorly built, distractors leak testwiseness cues the answerer can exploit as a last resort.

included: the homogeneous, lead-in-related, plausible-by-design nature of distractors as FACT
the consequence that surface plausibility is not evidence of correctness
the link to predict-then-match and to the flaw tiebreakers

pros.claim: Understanding distractors are built plausible reframes a sounds-right pull as a trap rather than a signal
pros.example: distrusting an option that matches a memorized phrase because word-repeat with the stem is a known writer cue

cons.claim: The flaw canon is verified via excerpts of the NBME guide, and the exact flaw-category count is from a secondary summary, so specifics are directional
cons.example: quoting a precise 13-flaw count as certain when only a secondary source gives the number

failure_modes: treating a plausible option as likely correct because it feels familiar
eliminating on surface plausibility instead of responsiveness to the lead-in
acceptance_tests: the node states distractors are homogeneous and lead-in-related and plausible by design (FACT), concludes surface plausibility is not evidence, and links to predict-then-match and the tiebreakers
revisit_triggers: the NBME flaw taxonomy is verified verbatim or its category count is confirmed
a distractor-analysis result changes which cues leak
an exam is found to be poorly built and cue-rich

base.update_signal: a flaw-taxonomy verification or a distractor-analysis result changes the trust model

nodes.definition: Prescribe the reading order for a single-best-answer item: read the lead-in (the last line, the actual question) first, then read the vignette — the learner then knows which data matter while reading the stem, instead of holding the whole vignette in memory and only then discovering what was asked [ESTIMATE — craft, medium-high confidence; synthesized from the NBME cover-the-options rule and widely taught test strategy]. For short stems, straight-through reading is fine and the lead-in-first move is skipped. The tactic pays off most on long clinical vignettes where the lead-in ('the next best step', 'the most likely diagnosis') tells the reader whether to weight history, exam or labs. It directly enables the predict-before-looking move: a focused lead-in read first is what lets the learner form an answer from the stem.

included: read-the-lead-in-first-then-the-vignette on long stems
the straight-through exception for short stems
why it enables predict-before-looking
excluded: the prediction and matching move itself

pros.claim: Reading the lead-in first tells the learner which vignette data to weight, cutting a wasted second pass
pros.example: seeing 'next best step' first and reading the vignette for the current stage rather than memorizing every datum

cons.claim: It is a craft tactic, not a measured effect, and on a short stem the lead-in-first move adds an extra jump for no gain
cons.example: flipping to the last line of a two-sentence item that reads faster straight through

failure_modes: reading a long vignette fully before discovering what was asked and rereading it
applying lead-in-first to a short stem where it only adds friction
acceptance_tests: the tactic prescribes lead-in-first-then-vignette on long stems, notes the short-stem exception, tags itself an estimate, and links to the predict move
revisit_triggers: observed timing data shows lead-in-first slows or speeds the learner
a stem-length threshold for switching modes is found
an exam's stems shorten or lengthen materially

base.update_signal: observed timing or a stem-length threshold revises the reading order

nodes.definition: Turn the cover-the-options rule into a solving move: after reading the stem, commit to a predicted answer before reading the options, then find the option that matches it. Because a well-built item's distractors are engineered plausible [DISTRACTOR_ENGINEERING], scanning the options first invites capture by a sounds-right trap; a pre-committed prediction immunizes the reader, who now looks for a match rather than being sold one [ESTIMATE — craft, medium-high; the NBME cover-the-options rule inverted into an answering tactic]. The move only works when the stem actually supports a prediction; when it does not, the learner falls through to systematic elimination. On the INBDE this is viable precisely because the one-best-answer model guarantees exactly one option is best on one dimension.

included: commit a predicted answer before viewing options then match it
why prediction immunizes against engineered distractors
the fall-through to elimination when no prediction is possible

pros.claim: A pre-committed prediction makes the learner match an answer instead of being sold a plausible distractor
pros.example: naming the likely diagnosis from the vignette, then selecting the option that states it and ignoring the near-miss distractors

cons.claim: Prediction fails on genuinely under-determined items and can anchor the learner to a wrong first guess
cons.example: fixating on a predicted answer not among the options and forcing a poor match instead of eliminating

failure_modes: scanning options first and being captured by an engineered distractor
anchoring on a wrong prediction and forcing it onto a non-matching option
acceptance_tests: the move commits a prediction before viewing options, explains the immunization against engineered distractors, and names the fall-through to elimination when prediction is impossible
revisit_triggers: an item type is found where prediction reliably misleads
observed accuracy data compares predict-first vs options-first
a distractor set defeats prediction on a recurring format

base.update_signal: accuracy data on predict-first vs options-first revises the move

nodes.definition: Define the elimination procedure used when no prediction is possible: strike options that are (a) true but non-responsive to the lead-in, (b) internally false, or (c) heterogeneous with the other options, leaving the responsive-and-true remainder. Elimination is on responsiveness to the lead-in, not on surface plausibility, because distractors are engineered plausible [DISTRACTOR_ENGINEERING] [ESTIMATE — craft, medium-high]. The single most common error it prevents is picking a true statement that does not answer the question actually asked. Writer-flaw testwiseness cues are used only as tiebreakers within the surviving set, never as the primary filter. On a negative stem the procedure inverts into an explicit true/false pass. Flagged-and-returned items re-enter this same elimination on the second pass.

included: strike true-but-non-responsive, internally-false and heterogeneous options
eliminate on responsiveness not surface plausibility
tiebreakers used only within the surviving set

pros.claim: Eliminating on responsiveness to the lead-in catches the true-but-non-responsive trap that plausibility-based elimination misses
pros.example: striking a factually true option that answers a different question than the lead-in asked

cons.claim: Elimination is slower than a clean prediction and, misapplied, can strike the responsive answer for a plausible distractor
cons.example: eliminating the correct terse option because a wordier distractor looks more complete

failure_modes: picking a true statement that does not answer the lead-in
eliminating on surface plausibility instead of responsiveness
acceptance_tests: the procedure strikes true-but-non-responsive, internally-false and heterogeneous options, eliminates on responsiveness not plausibility, and confines testwiseness cues to tiebreakers within the surviving set
revisit_triggers: a recurring error pattern shows a mis-eliminated answer class

base.update_signal: a recurring mis-elimination pattern or a tiebreaker revision updates the procedure

nodes.definition: Enumerate the writer-flaw testwiseness cues an answerer may use only as tiebreakers within a surviving option set: options with absolute terms (always, never) are usually wrong; the option that is the grammatical odd-one-out (does not follow from the lead-in) is usually wrong; the longest or most-detailed option is disproportionately the key; stem-option word repeats and a subset of options being collectively exhaustive point to the key [FACT — the cues are catalogued in the NBME flaw taxonomy via excerpts; ESTIMATE — using them to answer is craft]. The binding caveat: a well-built exam is deliberately scrubbed of these cues, so they help mainly on poorly built banks and must never override responsiveness-based elimination or a confident prediction. They are the last resort between two genuinely indistinguishable survivors.

included: the absolute-term, grammatical-odd-one-out, longest-option and word-repeat cues
the caveat that well-built exams are scrubbed of them
using them only as a last-resort tiebreaker

pros.claim: A ranked tiebreaker set breaks a genuine two-option deadlock without guessing blindly
pros.example: choosing the non-absolute survivor when two options are otherwise indistinguishable on a weak bank

cons.claim: On a well-built exam the cues are scrubbed out, so leaning on them misleads and can flip a correct elimination
cons.example: picking the longest option on a professionally built INBDE item where length carries no signal

failure_modes: using a testwiseness cue as the primary filter instead of a tiebreaker
trusting length or absolute-term heuristics on a well-built exam that scrubbed them
acceptance_tests: the node lists the absolute-term/odd-one-out/longest-option/word-repeat cues, states the well-built-exam scrub caveat, and confines them to last-resort tiebreakers
revisit_triggers: the target exam's build quality (cue-rich vs scrubbed) is characterized

nodes.definition: Handle negatively phrased lead-ins (EXCEPT / NOT / LEAST) by rewriting them mentally as 'mark each option true or false, then pick the one that is false (or the exception)'. The NBME canon discourages negative lead-ins because they measure reading care more than knowledge, so they are rare on well-built exams and common in weaker banks [FACT — NBME guidance via excerpts]; the rewrite converts the reading-care trap into a mechanical true/false pass that the knowledge can drive [ESTIMATE — craft]. The failure this prevents is the single most common careless error on these items: reading past the negation and selecting a true statement. It is a specialization of systematic elimination, applied whenever the lead-in is negated.

included: rewriting EXCEPT/NOT/LEAST as a per-option true/false pass then picking the false/exception
why negative stems are a reading-care trap (NBME)
the specialization-of-elimination framing

pros.claim: Rewriting a negative stem into a true/false pass removes the reading-care trap and lets knowledge drive
pros.example: labeling each option true/false and selecting the lone false one on an EXCEPT item instead of picking a true statement

cons.claim: The per-option true/false pass costs time, and on a well-built exam negative stems are rare so the drill is seldom needed
cons.example: spending a full true/false pass on a bank that almost never uses negative lead-ins

failure_modes: reading past the negation and selecting a true statement
forgetting to flip back to the false/exception option after the true/false pass
acceptance_tests: the node rewrites negative lead-ins as a per-option true/false pass picking the false/exception, cites the NBME reading-care rationale, and frames it as a specialization of elimination
revisit_triggers: the target bank's frequency of negative stems is characterized

base.update_signal: the bank's negative-stem frequency or a careless-error pattern updates the handling

nodes.definition: State the scoring fact that governs blanks: the INBDE has no penalty for guessing (pass/fail on a scaled 49-99 with pass = 75, where a scaled 75 is not 75% correct because scaling weighs item difficulty, discrimination and guessing susceptibility) [FACT — JCNDE results/scoring FAQ via excerpts]. Therefore every INBDE item is answered — a blank can only lose. For the TOEFL, no wrong-answer penalty is documented in any source seen this session, so MC items are treated the same way [ESTIMATE — no penalty found, not a positive confirmation]. The operational rule: after elimination or at the time cap, always record a best-remaining answer rather than leave a blank, and use any leftover time to revisit flagged items rather than to agonize before committing.

included: the INBDE no-guessing-penalty and scaled-75-is-not-75% FACT
the TOEFL no-documented-penalty ESTIMATE
the always-record-an-answer operational rule

pros.claim: A no-penalty exam makes a recorded best-guess strictly better than a blank on every item
pros.example: committing the best-remaining option at the time cap so a hard item can still score

cons.claim: The TOEFL no-penalty stance is an absence-of-evidence estimate, not a confirmed policy, so it should be re-checked
cons.example: assuming a TOEFL MC penalty is impossible when no source explicitly rules it in or out

failure_modes: leaving an item blank on a no-penalty exam
agonizing before committing instead of recording a best-guess and moving to flagged items
acceptance_tests: the rule states the INBDE no-guessing-penalty and scaled-75 fact, tags the TOEFL no-penalty stance an estimate, and mandates recording a best-remaining answer over a blank
revisit_triggers: ETS documents a TOEFL wrong-answer penalty
a scoring-scale change alters the guessing incentive

base.update_signal: a documented TOEFL penalty or a scoring-scale change updates the rule

nodes.definition: Prescribe the entry move for an INBDE itemset or case: scan the shared Patient Box once, systematically, in clinical order (demographics -> chief complaint -> meds/history -> findings) before item 1, then treat it as a per-item lookup table rather than rereading it for each item. The Patient Box is the INBDE's standardized patient-summary table, existing to enable direct skill assessment while avoiding unnecessary verbiage [FACT — INBDE Item Development Guide via excerpts]; the once-then-lookup tactic spends the shared-stimulus cost up front and then answers each item at near-standalone speed [ESTIMATE — craft]. Rereading the whole box per item is the main way a case set silently overspends the section clock.

included: scan the box once in clinical order before item 1
treat it as a per-item lookup table thereafter
the FACT of the box's structure and purpose
excluded: the independent-scoring rule for items in a set

pros.example: reading demographics/complaint/history/findings once, then jumping straight to the relevant line per item

cons.claim: A single up-front scan can miss a detail a later item hinges on, forcing a targeted reread
cons.example: overlooking a medication in the first scan that a drug-interaction item later depends on

failure_modes: rereading the whole Patient Box for every item and overspending the section clock
scanning too shallowly and missing a detail a later item needs
acceptance_tests: the move scans the box once in clinical order before item 1 and treats it as a per-item lookup, and states the box's structure/purpose as FACT
revisit_triggers: a case-set timing overrun traces to box rereading

base.update_signal: a case-set timing overrun or a box-template change updates the scan

nodes.definition: Set the cluster-level rule for INBDE itemsets and cases: an itemset is 3-6 items on a Patient Box only, a case is 3-6 items on a Patient Box plus an image or other stimulus [FACT], and the items within a set are independently scored — JCNDE writes sets so one item does not reveal another's answer and getting one wrong does not cascade [ESTIMATE — standard professional-exam construction, not verified verbatim]. The operational consequence: never revise an earlier answer merely to be 'consistent' with a later item, because there is no consistency reward and a later item's framing is not evidence about an earlier one. Work each item as a near-standalone off the once-scanned box, spending the shared-stimulus surplus up front.

included: the 3-6-item itemset/case definitions as FACT
independent scoring and the no-consistency-revision rule

nodes.definition: Read the cognitive level an item demands and match effort to it. The answerer uses this: a terse recall item ('which of the following is X') is a fast fact-lookup, while a clinical vignette ending in 'the next best step' is an apply/analyze decision that rewards the full stem-first, predict-then-eliminate procedure. Reading the level first prevents over-thinking a recall gate and under-working a decision item. A board-style bank is mostly apply/analyze, so the decision procedure is the default.

edge_cases.description: An earlier itemset answer is revised to be consistent with a later item's framing
edge_cases.trigger: a later item in the set seems to contradict an earlier answer
edge_cases.mitigation: treat set items as independently scored and keep the sound earlier answer rather than chasing consistency

edge_cases.description: The whole Patient Box is reread for every item in a case set, overspending the section clock
edge_cases.trigger: no single up-front box scan is done before item 1
edge_cases.mitigation: scan the box once in clinical order up front and use it as a per-item lookup thereafter

edge_cases.description: The legacy integrated read-listen-write note grid is applied to a current 2026 sitting that dropped integrated tasks
edge_cases.trigger: a legacy template is used without confirming the material's format era
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm legacy-vs-2026 via format-keying and apply the integrated grid only to confirmed legacy practice material

edge_cases.description: A WAD response summarizes the prompt and posts instead of contributing a position and engaging a classmate, losing the scored skill
edge_cases.trigger: the learner writes a neutral summary rather than a stance-plus-engagement contribution
edge_cases.mitigation: open with a clear position and engage a classmate by name per the WAD template, keeping >=100 words

edge_cases.description: A Write-an-Email response uses the wrong register for the recipient even though the content is correct
edge_cases.trigger: the greeting and requests are not matched to a professor-vs-friend recipient
edge_cases.mitigation: match the greeting register and hedging to the recipient first, then state purpose and requests

edge_cases.description: Weak syllables are over-articulated in Listen and Repeat, breaking the stress rhythm the task scores
edge_cases.trigger: the learner chases perfect function words instead of the prosodic shape
edge_cases.mitigation: chunk the sentence into 2-4 word stress groups and reproduce the stress pattern over perfect articles

edge_cases.description: The learner works past the flag cap on a hard standalone instead of banking a guess and moving on, starving later items
edge_cases.trigger: a single item exceeds its hard time cap
edge_cases.mitigation: record a best-guess, flag, and move at the cap, returning only if time remains

workflow.action: Identify the exam, format and stimulus in front of the learner
workflow.description: Determine INBDE vs TOEFL, the format (standalone/itemset/case/task-type) and the stimulus (none/box/image/audio), and legacy vs 2026
workflow.gate: the exam, format and stimulus are named and the legacy-vs-current era is decided before any procedure is chosen

workflow.description: For an INBDE MC item confirm 3-5 choices with exactly one best option on one dimension
workflow.gate: the one-best-answer model with the no-select-all negative finding is stated as FACT

workflow.action: Read the stem lead-in first, then the vignette
workflow.description: On a long stem read the lead-in first so the vignette is read for the data that matter
workflow.gate: the lead-in is read before the vignette on long stems and straight-through on short ones

workflow.action: Predict an answer before viewing the options
workflow.description: Commit a predicted answer from the stem, then match it among the options
workflow.gate: a prediction is committed before options are read whenever the stem supports one

workflow.description: Strike non-responsive, false and heterogeneous options; rewrite negative stems; use writer-flaw cues only as tiebreakers
workflow.gate: elimination is on responsiveness not plausibility and testwiseness cues are confined to tiebreakers

workflow.action: Scan the shared box and image once for case sets
workflow.description: Scan the Patient Box in clinical order and orient to any image before item 1, then treat both as lookups
workflow.gate: the box and image are scanned once up front and items are worked independently off them

workflow.action: Set per-item and per-task time budgets
workflow.description: Divide official counts into section times for the INBDE and TOEFL budgets, marking the split craft
workflow.gate: budgets are derived from official counts/times with the section totals load-bearing and the split tagged estimate

workflow.action: Apply the flag-and-move cap and never leave a blank
workflow.description: Hold a first-pass allowance and a hard cap; at the cap bank a best-guess, flag and move on
workflow.gate: a best-remaining answer is recorded at the cap and no item is left blank on a no-penalty exam

workflow.action: Drive the TOEFL productive tasks off note templates
workflow.description: Apply the WAD, email and Listen-and-Repeat templates inside their budgets
workflow.gate: each current-format productive task is driven by its template hitting the scored skill

workflow.action: Gate legacy integrated material by format
workflow.description: Apply the two-column integrated grid only to confirmed legacy practice material
workflow.gate: the integrated grid is used only on confirmed legacy material and never on a current sitting

workflow.description: Select the read/predict/eliminate/budget or task-template procedure from format+stimulus+time
workflow.gate: the playbook selects by the format in front of the learner and keeps craft tactics estimate and structural facts stated as fact

dominance_rules.rule: The format in front of the learner dominates any remembered strategy
dominance_rules.rationale: the same knowledge is tested through different mechanics across the INBDE and TOEFL and across legacy and 2026
dominance_rules.trigger: a procedure is chosen before the format and stimulus are identified
dominance_rules.action: identify exam + format + stimulus (and legacy-vs-current) first and key the procedure to them

dominance_rules.rule: A committed prediction dominates a plausible-sounding distractor
dominance_rules.rationale: distractors are engineered plausible to the non-master, so a sounds-right feeling is a built trap not a signal
dominance_rules.trigger: an option feels right on first scan before a prediction is committed
dominance_rules.action: predict the answer from the stem first and match it, distrusting surface plausibility

dominance_rules.rule: Responsiveness to the lead-in dominates surface plausibility in elimination
dominance_rules.rationale: the most common error is picking a true statement that does not answer the question asked
dominance_rules.trigger: an option is kept because it is plausible rather than responsive
dominance_rules.action: strike true-but-non-responsive options and keep only the responsive-and-true remainder

dominance_rules.rule: On a well-built exam, item content dominates testwiseness cues
dominance_rules.rationale: a professionally built exam is scrubbed of the flaw cues, so leaning on them misleads
dominance_rules.trigger: a flaw cue is used as the primary filter
dominance_rules.action: decide on prediction and responsiveness-based elimination and use cues only to break a genuine tie

dominance_rules.rule: Independent scoring dominates the consistency pull in a set
dominance_rules.rationale: itemset/case items are independently scored and one item does not reveal another's answer
dominance_rules.trigger: a later item tempts revising an earlier answer for consistency
dominance_rules.action: keep the sound earlier answer and work each item independently off the box

dominance_rules.rule: The no-guessing-penalty rule dominates any instinct to leave a blank
dominance_rules.rationale: on a no-penalty exam a recorded best-guess can only help and a blank can only lose
dominance_rules.trigger: an item is about to be left unanswered
dominance_rules.action: record a best-remaining answer on every item before the section closes

dominance_rules.rule: The per-item flag cap dominates the urge to crack a hard item
dominance_rules.rationale: one stuck item can starve several later answerable ones
dominance_rules.trigger: an item exceeds its hard time cap
dominance_rules.action: bank a best-guess, flag it, and move on, returning only if time remains

dominance_rules.rule: The current format dominates legacy templates
dominance_rules.rationale: the 2026 TOEFL dropped the integrated tasks and the essay, so legacy templates apply only to pre-2026 material
dominance_rules.trigger: a legacy integrated template is about to be used
dominance_rules.action: confirm the material's format era and apply the integrated grid only to legacy practice

dominance_rules.rule: The scored skill dominates volume in a productive task
dominance_rules.rationale: WAD is scored on contribution and engagement and the email on register, not on length
dominance_rules.trigger: a productive response is padded or summarized instead of hitting the scored skill
dominance_rules.action: hit the position-and-engagement (WAD) or register match (email) core before adding length

anti_rework_rules.rule: Identify the exam, format and stimulus before choosing any reading or elimination procedure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: running a mismatched procedure that has to be abandoned and redone once the format is noticed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the lead-in before the vignette on long stems
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reading a long vignette twice because the question was unknown on the first pass

anti_rework_rules.rule: Commit a prediction before viewing the options
anti_rework_rules.prevents: distractor capture that forces re-solving the item from scratch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Scan the Patient Box and image once up front for a case set
anti_rework_rules.prevents: per-item rereading of the shared stimulus that overspends the section clock

anti_rework_rules.rule: Derive per-item and per-task budgets from official counts before the section
anti_rework_rules.prevents: late-section time starvation from an unplanned pace

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm whether practice material is legacy or 2026 before drilling a template
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rehearsing an integrated task type the current exam no longer contains

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix a WAD position and classmate engagement before writing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a summary-style essay that has to be rewritten to score the contribution skill

anti_rework_rules.rule: Bank a best-remaining answer on every item on a no-penalty exam
anti_rework_rules.prevents: forfeited scorable marks from blanks left at time expiry

iteration_protocol.trigger: the official INBDE Candidate Guide section-level item and time numbers become fetchable and verifiable verbatim
iteration_protocol.action: replace the triangulated time table and re-derive the standalone and case per-item budgets and caps

iteration_protocol.trigger: ETS confirms the exact 2026 per-type item counts under the adaptive module
iteration_protocol.action: update the TOEFL per-task budgets and re-fit the productive-task templates to them

iteration_protocol.trigger: the exam format actually in front of the learner changes (a task added/dropped or a bank shifts legacy-to-current)
iteration_protocol.action: re-key the format-selection root and recompose the playbook branches

iteration_protocol.trigger: a TOEFL wrong-answer penalty is documented by ETS
iteration_protocol.action: revise the never-leave-a-blank rule for TOEFL and re-check the flag-and-move banking step

iteration_protocol.trigger: observed per-item timing or accuracy data from the learner's practice sessions arrives
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate the flag caps and re-compare predict-first vs elimination-first accuracy

iteration_protocol.trigger: the NBME item-writing flaw taxonomy is verified verbatim or its category count is confirmed
iteration_protocol.action: update the testwiseness tiebreakers and the distractor-engineering trust model

iteration_protocol.trigger: legacy TOEFL practice material is fully retired from the learner's bank
iteration_protocol.action: retire the legacy integrated grid and route all TOEFL work through the current-format templates

priority_rationale: Format-keying, the one-best-answer model and distractor engineering come first because every reading and elimination move depends on knowing the format in front of the learner and why a plausible option cannot be trusted; the stem-first read, predict-before-looking, systematic elimination, negative-stem handling and the no-guessing-penalty rule next, because they are the core single-item procedure; the Patient-Box scan, case-cluster strategy and image orientation then specialize that procedure for grouped items; the time-budget model, the INBDE and TOEFL budgets and flag-and-move follow, because they pace every procedure to the section clock; the Bloom-level read and the WAD, email, legacy-integrated and Listen-and-Repeat templates apply the procedure to productive and cognitively varied tasks; and the strategy-selection playbook comes last because it composes format, stimulus and time into one per-item answering decision.
